findings.message: current-pm.mjs validateAdmissionRecord/remoteAdmissionStatus accepts syntactically coherent completion without the required remote proof chain. It checks remote.version, optional slots only if present, completion target/branch/commit, then marks COMPLETE when commit is ancestor of HEAD. A record can omit source publication/merge proof, integration_evidence finalization, closure/handoff-repair proof and terminal artifact identities yet release admission. This directly violates initial-observations admission-proof ('syntactically valid completion.status alone cannot release hold').

closure/repair provider interruption is not implemented. reconcileExecutingAttempt is called only by source publish/merge. Closure executeProviderAttempt leaves thrown executing slots stuck; closure reconcile proves Git without settling the slot. Repair uses a bespoke runner that unconditionally allocates a new token whenever effect is null, overwriting an executing active token and permitting a second write; repair reconcile also never settles slots. This violates the all-stage prepared/executing/observed and read-only recovery contract. Fresh-process lost execution must remain UNKNOWN absent exact effect adoption; same-process ended+exact absence may replay the same token.

raced closure preimage checks compare only file text/hash, not Git mode. A concurrent 100644→100755 mode change on a P/E/H path has identical committedText, is allowed as an in-scope changed path, then wrapper restores H's mode; code accepts it, overwriting the advanced-base entry despite exact-preimage requirement.

H2 adoption compares only captureGitAnchor().protected_hash; unlike closure/completion it retains no protectedIgnoredEntries checkout proof, so worktree-local ignored protected metadata can drift between prepare/adopt without refusal.

maybeSupersedeSourceAttempt changes old.disposition/superseded_by then refreshAttempt(old), but deliberately leaves slot.effect unchanged. Its effect.attempt_identity therefore points to the pre-mutation identity that no retained attempt now has. The supersession proof omits required predecessor attempt/effect identities and validateProviderSlot never checks reciprocal links/effect-to-attempt binding. After successor success old effect pointer is replaced, so old identity is not durably recoverable.

rebase proof sets rebaseBase=parents[0] of final rebased commit and checks only rebaseBase..mergeCommit; for legitimate multi-commit source rebase, that parent is the preceding rebased source commit, so earlier rebased commits are outside bounded-path proof. Established premerge base is retained in merge attempt observation and should anchor the whole first-parent range. Current tests use one source commit.

claimCurrentPm checks remote admission before entering transact but does not repeat it inside the transaction, contrary to the approved T05B admission dispatch. A remote record can become applicable in another checkout after the precheck and before the story write, and the claim then commits without the required hold.

validateRemoteEnvelope validates only provider-slot shells and retry range, while prepareRemoteClosureCheckout trusts truthy integration_evidence.finalized/finalization. It does not validate the identified finalization or its binding to the current snapshot, gates, review and verification; a malformed/rebound record can therefore enter P/E/H closure with forged finalized evidence.

source merge interruption treats `MERGE_PENDING` as an absence state eligible for same-process replay (`mergeRemoteSource` passes `absenceStates: ['MERGE_PENDING']`). The frozen dispatch says replay requires exact provider absence and that open/queued remains pending; an open/queued PR may already retain a provider merge request, so it cannot prove no effect and must not authorize a second merge write. This needs to stay pending/read-only unless exact merge effect is adopted.

prepareRemoteHandoff does not require an adopted story-closure E. remotePrepareArtifact assigns `parent = closure.commit`, which can be null, persists the handoff pending record, then writes H bytes. Adoption can never accept a real commit whose parent equals null, and the dirty H write then prevents preparing E, leaving the workflow wedged. The public operation should refuse before record/file mutation until E is adopted.

prepareHandoffRepair is not resumable across its own durable-preparation/file-write boundary. It first records a prepared attempt in withRecord, writes H2 bytes afterward, but every repeated prepare rejects whenever latest exists without race_proof. A crash after record persistence and before/while writeArtifact therefore cannot apply the retained pending after-image or return its token; the accepted prepare/adopt interruption model is broken.

summary: Reviewed the complete frozen T05B scope at snapshot 89d174d040b90ceeb474576fc53939086084ecbd1466be08f0653a51c13fac1d against the original three acceptance criteria, approved remote contracts and dispatch notes, all 13 initial observations, the rebase ruling, retained Fable triage, production wiring and frozen tests. The declared gates passed unchanged: npm test 340/340 in 563301.498166ms and validate PASS. The CLI and installed complete-operation routing are connected, fetch/push identity is enforced, empty rebase commits are correctly permitted, required-check absence is explicitly diagnosed, and retained strict PR/CLEAN behavior matches policy. The eleven unresolved major findings leave AC1, AC2 and AC3 unproved despite the passing gates.
